 LIVE NOW Save Share Comments Gold, Silver Prices Today Highlights : Gold jumps over 1% as falling oil prices ease inflation fears
 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 10, 2026, 06:34:43 IST SUMMARY Gold, Silver Prices Today Live Updates: Gold and silver prices have resumed their upward movement, although commodity experts and market analysts expect volatility in both precious metals to continue in the near term. Both metals have witnessed a sharp surge in prices over the past year. While gold benefits from its safe-haven appeal amid global uncertainty, silver has gained additional momentum from rising industrial demand, contributing to the rally in prices. 
 However, expectations of a more measured approach by the US Federal Reserve towards interest rate cuts, coupled with profit booking at elevated levels, have triggered corrections from the record highs. Despite these short-term fluctuations, analysts believe the broader bullish trend in both gold and silver remains firmly in place. 
 What are the latest MCX gold and silver rates? How do spot gold and silver prices compare in the physical bullion market today? What price targets are analysts projecting for the two precious metals this year? Track TOI’s live coverage on gold, silver prices today: Live Events 
 06:30 (IST) Nov 10 Gold Rate Today: India's gold jewellery demand hits 99.9 tonnes in Q3, most since late 2024 India's gold jewellery demand was 99.9 tons in the third quarter, the most since the fourth quarter of last year, according to World Gold Council data cited by Reuters. China's jewellery demand rose to 71.9 tons in the third quarter, up from 55.7 tons in the second. Lower prices in recent months are likely to boost jewellery demand further as key festivals approach in India. 05:27 (IST) Nov 10 Gold Rate Today: Gold jumps 1.2% to $4,116 as dollar eases, crude fall cools inflation fears Spot gold rose 1.2% to $4,116.15 per ounce as the dollar eased and lower crude prices eased inflation jitters, with markets awaiting US inflation data due Tuesday. US gold futures gained 1.2% to $4,125.40.
 Oil dropped sharply after President Donald Trump downplayed the likelihood of renewed strikes on Iran, though attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz kept supply concerns in focus. Traders see an 82.2% chance of a December Fed hike, CME's FedWatch showed.
 03:30 (IST) Nov 10 Silver Rate Today: Silver jumps 1.6% to $52.69 as metals rally on softer dollar Spot silver rose 1.6% to $52.69 per ounce, tracking gold higher as a softer dollar and lower crude prices eased inflation concerns. 01:30 (IST) Nov 10 Platinum Rate Today: Platinum gains 2.1% to $1,564.95, palladium up 0.2% to $1,025.46 Spot platinum climbed 2.1% to $1,564.95 per ounce while palladium added 0.2% to $1,025.46, with the broader precious-metals complex rallying on a weaker dollar and falling crude prices. 00:45 (IST) Nov 10 Silver Rate Today: Bengaluru silver closes at Rs 2,00,300 per kilogram Silver closed at Rs 2,00,300 per kilogram in the Bengaluru bullion market on Monday, according to PTI. 23:30 (IST) Nov 09 Gold Rate Today: Bengaluru gold closes at Rs 13,650 per gram for 22K, Rs 14,890 for 24K Gold closed at Rs 13,650 per gram for 22-carat and Rs 14,890 per gram for 24-carat in the Bengaluru bullion market on Monday, according to PTI.  Lite Challenge Play Now 22:30 (IST) Nov 09 Gold prices today: Gold prices seen bullish by year-end amid dollar uncertainty, falling oil prices and strong investment demand: Analysts Gold prices are expected to remain bullish towards the end of 2026, supported by uncertainty surrounding the US dollar, falling crude oil prices and strong investment demand, with analysts pointing to central-bank purchases, expectations of monetary easing and geopolitical developments as additional factors supporting the precious metal.
 Amit Gupta, Senior Research Analyst at Kedia Advisory Services, said several fundamental factors could support gold over the coming months, including Federal Reserve policy, central-bank purchases, gold exchange-traded fund (ETF) inflows and geopolitical uncertainty.
 “Central-bank buying remains one of the strongest structural supports,” Gupta said, adding that a shift towards monetary easing or indications that the rate-hiking cycle had ended could reduce US Treasury yields and the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold. 
 He noted that the Federal Reserve held its target interest rate at 3.75-4.00 per cent on October 28, 2026, making its December policy decision and accompanying guidance important for gold prices.
 On central-bank demand, Gupta cited purchases of 321 tonnes in Q3 2026, up 42 per cent year-on-year, taking January-September purchases to 675 tonnes, a 6 per cent increase. China and Poland were among the leading disclosed buyers. Global gold ETFs attracted 211 tonnes during Q3, taking total holdings to a record 4,256 tonnes.
 Gupta also highlighted an 8 per cent year-on-year decline in global gold recycling to 314 tonnes in Q3, which could support the supply-demand balance. He advised existing long-term investors to maintain their strategic allocation rather than panic-selling during corrections, while recommending that fresh investors adopt staggered purchases through gold ETFs.
 However, Gupta cautioned that a hawkish Federal Reserve, stronger US economic data, rising crude oil prices, ETF outflows and profit-booking could trigger another correction. He identified $3,800 as an important support level, warning that a weekly close below it would weaken the recovery outlook. The $4,155-$4,240 range represents a key resistance zone.
 Anindya Banerjee, Head of Research at Kotak Neo, expects international gold prices to rise to $4,400-$4,450 per ounce by year-end, with domestic prices potentially touching Rs 1.50 lakh on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX).
 “By year-end we expect gold prices to rise from $4,100 to $4,400-$4,450 and around Rs 1.50 lakh on MCX,” Banerjee told ANI.
Banerjee identified political crises in the United States that could undermine confidence in the US dollar, reduced risks of war in West Asia and falling crude oil prices as factors supporting gold. He said lower oil prices could reduce the risk of aggressive interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve.
Dinesh Somani, Proprietor of ProIntellitrade Services brokerage, also expects a recovery in gold prices, projecting international prices of $4,450-$4,500 by year-end. He said international gold had declined from a recent high of $4,700 to around $3,860 before recovering towards $4,120.
 “I think probably $3,860 should be the bottom for near term, at least for this year end. Upside target again expecting around $4,450 to $4,500 levels,” Somani told ANI.
 On the domestic market, Somani identified Rs 1,38,000 as the recent low and expects prices to find a near-term bottom around Rs 1,40,500-Rs 1,41,000, with an upside target of Rs 1,49,000. He said he did not expect prices to breach the recent low of Rs 1,38,000.
 Somani attributed the price movement partly to geopolitical tensions and said a V-shaped recovery could be possible. He added that the Dollar Index was hovering around 102, while the rupee had appreciated from around 97 to below 94 against the US dollar and could move towards 92, potentially putting pressure on domestic gold prices. He also expects crude oil prices to decline further.
 Gold recovered from its 2026 low of $3,869.85 recorded on October 30, after reaching a record high of $5,594.82 on January 29. (ANI)
 21:30 (IST) Nov 09 Gold Rate Today: Gold climbs more than 1% as inflation fears ease on lower crude prices Gold prices climbed more than 1% on Monday as the dollar eased and inflationary jitters took a back seat due to lower crude oil prices, while markets awaited US inflation data later this week.
 Spot gold was up 1.5% at $4,126.25 per ounce by 9:26 a.m. ET (1426 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery also gained 1.5% to $4,135.50.
 "We're seeing a lower US dollar index on this first day of the trading week," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange.
 "We're seeing lower crude oil prices today that suggest receding inflationary fears — that's positive for the gold and silver markets, on ideas that lessening inflation fears will allow the central banks to lean easier on their monetary policies."
 21:06 (IST) Nov 09 Gold rebounds above $4,100 as global bullion prices recover International gold prices rose nearly 1 per cent to $4,100 an ounce on Monday, recovering from last week's brief decline. Investors assessed stronger US employment data against softer Treasury yields and expectations of easing geopolitical tensions. Continued gold purchases by China's central bank, which extended its buying streak to 24 consecutive months, also supported the market, PTI reported.
 19:44 (IST) Nov 09 Silver remains unchanged at Rs 1.92 lakh per kg in Delhi Silver prices remained unchanged at Rs 1,92,500 per kg in the national capital on Monday, even as gold staged a recovery. In international markets, however, spot silver gained more than 1 per cent to trade at $52.58 an ounce, according to PTI. 19:43 (IST) Nov 09 Gold Rate Today: Gold's short-term volatility contrasts with long-term bullishness Gold appears to be finding a floor around $4,000 an ounce as it battles competing short-term influences and a shift in how it is traded.
 The spot price of the precious metal ended at $4,065.63 an ounce on November 6, having recovered from its low so far this year of $3,869.85 on October 30.
 Gold's recovery from its most recent drop below $4,000 an ounce came after it performed a similar trick in July, when it dipped on several occasions below the key psychological level, only to recover.
 The yellow metal also came close to dropping below $4,000 an ounce in March, when it slipped to $4,097.99 on March 23, as it corrected amid profit-taking after reaching a record high of $5,594.82 on January 29.
 It has been a fairly wild ride for gold in 2026 and much of the commentary has focused on how it appears to have largely lost its traditional role as a hedge against inflation and geopolitical turmoil.
 Rather it seems that gold has witnessed more speculative trading, although much of the froth and hot money has been washed out in recent months as it flirted with a break below $4,000 an ounce.
 However, gold remains in short-term limbo, caught between competing influences and vulnerable to swings in either direction.
 18:22 (IST) Nov 09 Gold rises Rs 600 to Rs 1.46 lakh per 10 grams in Delhi Gold prices recovered in the national capital on Monday, rising Rs 600 to Rs 1,46,900 per 10 grams, compared with Rs 1,46,300 on Friday. Easing crude oil prices and a firm global trend supported the recovery, while recent price corrections also encouraged physical purchases during the Diwali festive season, PTI reported. 18:13 (IST) Nov 09 Gold bounces back in Delhi as easing oil prices, global gains support bullion Gold staged a modest recovery on Monday, with prices rising by Rs 600 to Rs 1,46,900 per 10 grams in the national capital as weak crude rates and a firm global trend lifted investor sentiment.
 The 99.9 per cent pure yellow metal closed at Rs 1,46,300 per 10 grams on Friday.

Gold, Silver Prices Today Live Updates: Gold has traditionally been regarded as a safe-haven investment, attracting investors during periods of economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Developments in the global economy over the past few years have kept the precious metal in the spotlight, driving prices higher. The trade war initiated by US President Donald Trump heightened concerns over the global economic outlook, while rising geopolitical tensions further strengthened gold's appeal as a preferred investment option worldwide.
Central banks across the world, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), have also increased their gold purchases in recent years. The RBI has steadily added several tonnes of the yellow metal to its reserves, significantly raising gold's share in India's foreign exchange reserves. According to the latest World Gold Council data, India currently has the world's eighth-largest gold reserves, estimated at around 880 tonnes. The United States tops the global rankings, with gold holdings nearly ten times India's.
